verses.label: Doha 1
originalText: श्रीगुरु चरन सरोज रज, निज मनु मुकुरु सुधारि।
बरनउँ रघुबर बिमल जसु, जो दायकु फल चारि॥
transliteration: Shri guru charan saroj raj, nij manu mukuru sudhaari
Baranau Raghubar bimal jasu, jo daayaku phal chaari
verses.existingMeaning: Having cleaned the mirror of my mind with the dust of my teacher’s lotus feet, I describe the pure glory of Lord Rama, which grants the four aims of life.
verses.existingExplanation: The “mirror” is the mind: pride, confusion, and selfishness can cloud our understanding. Honouring the teacher represents humility and readiness to learn. The four aims are dharma, living rightly; artha, earning and sustaining life; kama, love and fulfilment; and moksha, spiritual freedom.

verses.label: Doha 2
originalText: बुद्धिहीन तनु जानि कै, सुमिरौं पवन-कुमार।
बल बुद्धि बिद्या देहु मोहि, हरहु कलेस बिकार॥
transliteration: Buddhiheen tanu jaanike, sumirau Pavan Kumaar
Bal buddhi vidyaa dehu mohi, harahu kalesh vikaar
verses.existingMeaning: Knowing the limits of my understanding, I remember Hanuman, the son of the Wind God. Give me strength, sound judgement, and knowledge, and remove my suffering and harmful tendencies.
verses.existingExplanation: The prayer asks for more than physical power. It asks for the courage to act, the wisdom to choose well, and the knowledge to understand. Calling oneself “without wisdom” expresses humility before the divine.

verses.label: Chaupai 1
verses.existingMeaning: Glory to Hanuman, whose knowledge and virtues are as vast as an ocean. Glory to the lord of the vanaras, whose greatness shines through the three worlds.
verses.existingExplanation: The vanaras are the monkey-like beings who help Rama in the Ramayana. The three worlds broadly mean the heavenly, earthly, and lower realms. Hanuman is praised first for wisdom and character, showing that his greatness includes much more than strength.

verses.label: Chaupai 2
verses.existingMeaning: You are Rama’s messenger and the home of incomparable strength. You are Anjana’s son, also known as the son of the Wind God.
verses.existingExplanation: These names describe Hanuman’s parentage and divine connection. “Rama’s messenger” also expresses his purpose: he uses his abilities to serve Rama faithfully.

verses.existingExplanation: “Bajrangi” refers to his thunderbolt-like strength. The second line turns attention inward: a person may need help overcoming confused or destructive thoughts as much as an outside enemy.

verses.existingExplanation: Bharata is deeply beloved by Rama. Comparing Hanuman with him recognises Hanuman as someone held close in love, beyond his role as a servant or messenger.

verses.label: Closing Doha
originalText: पवनतनय संकट हरन, मंगल मूरति रूप।
राम लखन सीता सहित, हृदय बसहु सुर भूप॥
transliteration: Pavantanay sankat haran, mangal moorat roop
Raam Lakhan Seetaa sahit, hriday basahu sur bhoop
verses.existingMeaning: O son of the Wind God, remover of troubles and embodiment of blessing, dwell in my heart together with Rama, Lakshmana, and Sita.
verses.existingExplanation: The final prayer gathers the whole hymn into one wish: that Hanuman and those he loves remain present within the devotee. It asks for an inward life shaped by courage, compassion, loyalty, and faith.
